verdicts.reason: Both use the same two-column layout, and both share the same flaws. The body copy is jammed directly under the headline with no divider or breathing room. The orange divider rule ends up orphaned above the CTA in the right column. The CTA column floats in empty navy with dead space below it. A keeps the original's full-width white header band, but the logo sits off-centre at the left. B cuts the white band off at about two-thirds of the width, so it reads as a broken, truncated panel with a stray navy notch at top right. That damages brand fidelity and balance more than A's off-centre logo.
